In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
Porphyra purpuraea is a K+-accumulating, Cl−-accumulating, Na+-excreting species.
Porphyra purpurae has a high K+/Na+ discrimination ratio, with K+ being actively accumulated, and a high Cl−/Na+ discrimination ratio.

the ionic relations of P. purpurea are consistent with the presence of a ‘primary pump’ which is electrogenic, Na+-independent and Cl−-dependent, and which is responsible for the maintenance of an internal concentration of K+ greater than the external concentration.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the ionic relations of P. purpurea are typical of a marine alga with respect to the relative concentrations of K+, Na+, Cl−, and Ca2+ and the fluxes of the major ions.
the ionic relations of P. purpurea are similar to those of other red algae and to those of green plants.
the plasmalemmal permeability characteristics of P. purpurea are similar to those of higher plants, with the additional features of a K+/Na+ discrimination and a Cl−/Na+ discrimination.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the membrane potential is not a simple reflection of the ion gradients, but rather the result of the interplay between active ion pumps, ion channels, and ion exchange.

the membrane of the red alga Porphyra is a highly selective barrier that discriminates between the three major inorganic ions, and the membrane potential is maintained by an electrogenic Na+-H+ exchanger and K+-Cl− cotransporter.
